1edcblp:562: The core value of the Claude Code architecture lies in transforming "wild functions" into "controlled objects with complete runtime semantics." This means the tool layer is not simply exposing function calls, but contains a complete runtime with execution context, permission checks, and state management. ^(raw/articles/claude-code-architecture-analysis) Six modules form a layered architecture: the entry chain handles process initialization and state separation; the REPL acts as a runtime console for continuous user interaction; the Query Loop drives continuous execution in a state-machine pattern, supporting Compact compression and recovery; the Tool Runtime is the convergence point for cross-cutting complexity; the Permission System provides a complete decision chain rather than simple pop-ups; and the Task abstraction gives multi-Agent a unified task-reclaim mechanism. ^(raw/articles/claude-code-architecture-analysis) The most noteworthy design principle of this architecture is "external dynamic, internal convergence" — MCP/Skills/Plugins can be dynamically extended, but internal module boundaries remain clear and dependencies stable. This directly answers why many Agent systems are strong at the demo stage but begin to "deform" once tools multiply: they lack a runtime architecture that truly absorbs complexity. ^(raw/articles/claude-code-architecture-analysis)
